# Arnaud Wiehe

> Cybersecurity executive, author, and international speaker specializing in AI governance, emerging technologies, and digital risk.

## Who

Arnaud Wiehe is Managing Director of Information Security and AI Governance. He holds AIGP, CISSP, CCSP, CISM, CISA, and CIPP/E certifications. With over two decades of experience, he helps organizations translate complex technological change into clear, actionable business strategy.

## Topics

- AI governance and risk management
- Cybersecurity leadership and strategy
- Emerging technology risk (AI, quantum, XR)
- Board-level technology governance
- Agent governance and runtime controls
- EU AI Act compliance
- CISO leadership and operating models

## Books

- **The Book on Cybersecurity**: How Nontechnical Corporate Leaders and Boards Can Manage in a Scary Digital World
- **Emerging Tech, Emerging Threats**: A Cybersecurity Guide for Innovative Leaders

## Speaking

GITEX Global Dubai, World Summit AI, Economist Metaverse Summit, ISACA Risk Events, Next IT Security Stockholm. Topics: AI governance, cybersecurity strategy, emerging technology leadership.

## Articles

The complete article index is available at https://arnaudwiehe.com/articles/.

Selected source material:

- [An OpenClaw Email Agent Failed a Phishing Test](https://arnaudwiehe.com/articles/openclaw-email-agent-phishing-test/) — agent identity, phishing, data access, and controls outside the prompt.
- [AI Agent Debt — The Governance Gap Nobody Is Measuring](https://arnaudwiehe.com/articles/ai-agent-debt/) — accumulated governance and operational risk from deployed agents.
- [Before You Scale AI Agents, Give Them an Identity, a Privilege Boundary, and a Kill Switch](https://arnaudwiehe.com/articles/agent-governance-kill-switch/) — identity, least privilege, runtime boundaries, and termination controls.
- [Your AI Vendor Questionnaire Doesn't Ask the Questions That Matter Anymore](https://arnaudwiehe.com/articles/ai-vendor-questionnaire-obsolete/) — modern AI third-party risk and assurance questions.
- [Prompt Injection: Why Runtime Controls Beat Policy Checklists](https://arnaudwiehe.com/articles/prompt-injection-runtime-controls/) — prompt injection risk and enforced runtime controls.
- [When Export Control Comes for AI Models](https://arnaudwiehe.com/articles/export-control-ai-models/) — geopolitical and supply-chain implications for AI providers and enterprise buyers.
